subject.title: fix(tts): validate maxLength is a positive finite number

question: Should the public TTS runtime facade begin rejecting previously accepted invalid numeric values, and if so what exact supported range and upgrade behavior should plugins receive?
rationale: The patch changes observable plugin-facing failure behavior while the current user command already enforces a different 100–4096 range; code review cannot safely choose the permanent API contract without owner intent.

options.title: Define and enforce one facade contract
options.body: Recommended: document the accepted range at the public facade, align command and writer checks, add compatibility coverage, and land the guard with real-run proof.

options.title: Keep validation at command input
options.body: Retain the established command-level range and avoid introducing a new throwing behavior in the public facade until a concrete external caller requires it.

options.title: Add a versioned migration path
options.body: If invalid plugin writes must now fail, preserve an explicit compatibility/deprecation path and notify plugin authors before enforcing it.

recommendation.title: Define and enforce one facade contract
recommendation.body: Recommended: document the accepted range at the public facade, align command and writer checks, add compatibility coverage, and land the guard with real-run proof.
